sources.entry: Webhook Debugger, Logger & API Mocking Suite | Self-hosted webhook debugging and API mocking suite with live inspection, replay, forwarding, and signature verification

summary.one_liner: A self-hosted or Apify-hosted webhook debugger that generates temporary endpoints, captures and searches incoming requests, replays or forwards them, and mocks callback responses.
summary.what_it_does: Generates temporary webhook URLs (1-50 per run) with configurable retention and captures the full request envelope: method, headers, query, body, response status and headers, size, latency, and IP. Captured events are queryable through a DuckDB-backed /logs endpoint with pagination, and can be streamed live over Server-Sent Events at /log-stream. Stored events can be replayed to a different target URL, and all incoming traffic can be forwarded to another destination with retries and circuit breaking. The endpoint can mock downstream behavior by returning custom status codes, bodies, headers, and artificial latency. Security options include an authKey, an IP/CIDR allowlist, sensitive header masking, and provider signature verification for Stripe, Shopify, GitHub, Slack, or custom signatures. Optional JSON Schema validation and sandboxed inline JavaScript transforms run before storage, and Slack or Discord alerts can fire on error, 4xx, 5xx, timeout, or signature_invalid events.
use_cases: Inspect webhook payloads from Stripe, GitHub, Shopify, Slack, or custom services
Debug webhook integrations without tunneling localhost
Replay failed callbacks against staging after a fix
Simulate slow or failing downstream responses for client testing
Forward test traffic to another service while keeping an audit log
Verify provider webhook signatures during development
stack: Isolated vm worker threads for custom scripts
notable: Full request capture with a searchable /logs API and live SSE stream
Replay and forwarding with retries, timeouts, and circuit breaker
Built-in provider signature verification (Stripe, Shopify, GitHub, Slack, custom)
Sandboxed custom JavaScript transforms that run before events are stored
Runs on Apify or as a self-hosted Node.js/Docker service with hot-reloadable input
caveats: Generated webhook URLs are public unless authKey, allowedIps, or signature verification is enabled
Retention is limited to 1-168 hours and the actor is positioned for testing, not permanent ingress or long-term storage
Apify pay-per-event pricing listed at about $10 per 1,000 captured webhooks
